You were reshuffled into a ministry that does not exist.

170.name: Party Leader
170.description: Lead a party in the assembly: hold the benches together and the leadership against rivals.

success: The benches voted as one, which never happens.
A rival defected to you with a whole faction.
Your speech was quoted in every paper, correctly.
The polls moved your way for a reason you could name.
Party funds came in faster than the scandals.
partial: The party held, but only just and only today.
Your motion failed by the width of one absent colleague.
A donor asked for something small, for now.
You were heckled, and heckled back rather well.
The manifesto grew two new promises nobody costed.
failure: Three members voted with the government by mistake.
A leadership challenge was rumoured, then scheduled.
Your slogan was mocked on the radio all afternoon.
The treasurer resigned to spend more time with the accounts.
Your own backbench leaked the strategy meeting.
disaster: The party split down the middle during your speech.
A tape surfaced. You are on it.
Your deputy launched a new party that afternoon, with your staff.
The donors asked for their money back, with interest.
You lost the confidence vote in your own party room.

171.name: Legislator
171.description: Sit in the chamber or the electoral college: read the bills, cast the votes, keep the seat.

success: Your amendment survived three readings intact.
You read the whole bill, which made you the expert.
Your vote decided the division, and you voted well.
A constituent wrote to thank you, in legible handwriting.
The committee adopted your report without changes.
partial: You voted, then read the bill, in that order.
Your amendment passed as a footnote.
The session ran long and your question was not reached.
You were present, which the record will show.
A lobbyist took you to lunch and only nearly succeeded.
failure: You voted the wrong way on a bill you had co-sponsored.
Your speech was delivered to three members and a clerk.
The whip was displeased and said so in writing.
You missed the division bell by a corridor.
Your office misplaced a petition with a thousand names.
disaster: You were caught asleep during a roll call.
Your expenses were read aloud in the chamber.
A bill you wrote did the exact opposite of its title.
You were expelled from the sitting for a remark about a colleague's hat.
The chamber voted to censure you, unanimously, including you.
